title: stackward run journal v1
description: The record `stackward apply` keeps of one run, at /var/backups/stackward/<run_id>/journal.json (mode 0600). It is rewritten atomically after every file and command, so a run that dies leaves a journal with status running. `stackward undo --run <run_id>` reads it. File content is redacted; the hashes are of the real bytes. Adding an optional field is not a breaking change; removing or renaming a field, or changing a meaning, needs journal.v2.

run_id.description: The UTC start time and six random hex digits.

status.description: running: in progress, or the run died. ok: every selected step is applied. failed: a step failed and the run stopped there. undone: stackward undo reversed the run.

undone_at.description: When stackward undo finished, RFC 3339 UTC.

plan.description: The plan file the run applied.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the plan file as read.

selected.description: The selected step ids, in plan order.

backup_dir.description: Where the run keeps the old copy of every file it overwrote, at the file's own path below this directory.

transaction.description: Optional. Present when the run was an access-critical transaction (its run id is the transaction id). The state file /var/lib/stackward/transaction.json (schema/transaction.v1.json) is the authority; this copy stays with the run.

status.description: open: applied and validated, waiting for stackward confirm. confirmed: the change stays. rolled-back: undone by the timer, a failed check, a failed step or stackward undo --transaction. rollback-failed: the undo failed part way. aborted: the timer could not be armed and nothing changed.

deadline.description: When the rollback timer fires, RFC 3339 UTC.

timer_unit.description: The transient systemd units (NAME.timer and NAME.service).

cause.description: Why it rolled back: timer (no confirm before the deadline), validation (a check after the steps failed), apply-failed (a step failed), manual (stackward undo --transaction).

checks.description: The checks run after the steps: sshd -t, sshd -T and ss.

status.description: applied: ran to the end. failed: stopped part way (see files and commands). already: the check found it in place and nothing ran. not-run: an earlier step failed first.

restart_pending.description: Optional. True from the moment a file of the step is written until its commands have run: the files are in place but the restart or load did not finish. The next apply finishes it first. Absent means not pending.

step.description: The plan step as applied, in the shape of a step of plan.v1 (schema/plan.v1.json), with old and new file content redacted. Undo authorizes it again and runs its undo commands.

changed.description: False when the file already held the new content, or the write did not happen (validation failed).

mode.description: Permission the file was written with, octal.

uid.description: Owner it was written with; -1 when left to the writing process (root).

backup.description: The copy of the old file under backup_dir (replace only).

orig.description: FILE.orig (replace only). It is written once, the first time stackward replaces the file, and never replaced.

orig_created.description: True when this run wrote FILE.orig.

undone.description: Set by stackward undo once the file is restored or removed.

kind.description: validate: checks a staged file before it is moved into place (the staged path is the last argument). before: a step command before the edits (a package install, after apt-get update when the lists were stale). command: a step command after the edits. undo: run by stackward undo. check: a transaction check after the steps ran (sshd -t, sshd -T, ss).

args.description: Argument vector, run without a shell.

exit_code.description: -1 when the command could not start or was killed.

output.description: stdout and stderr, redacted, at most 4 KiB.
